TraceRook native app walkthrough — 60 seconds

Recorded with labeled demo data. No real commands execute; Codex scenes are simulations.

Meet TraceRook, a native Mac companion for reviewing risky coding agent actions.

The dashboard brings sessions, findings, and pending reviews together. This walkthrough uses labeled demo data, with no real commands executing.

Open a session to see the task and its timeline. Here, the sample shows a credential upload blocked by local policy.

Each finding explains the proposed action, its evidence, and its relationship to your task. Local rules retain authority over critical denials.

Higher-risk actions can wait for your review. The native panel shows the task, evidence, exact action binding, and a deadline.

Choose Block and the simulated review resolves immediately. Allow once applies to one exact action; the coding agent still controls its own permissions.

TraceRook Cloud uses Anthropic Claude. Explore the invited Mac beta at tracerook.dev.
